refuted_claims:
1. CLAIM (title and verdict_cn): "现有的人写任务说明已接近'任何通用文字'能达到的上限" / "what a generic rule can reach is about 0-3 points".
- Checked: the cal-1 arms file (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dulin-Documents-Paper-SkillOpt/e7258b97-b430-4dd5-959d-eb871e7c777f/scratchpad/feas/D9/arms-cal1-searchqa.json) and docs/results-and-lessons.md.
- None of the 11 texts is "TC + a rule":
  - ids-full is the TC;
  - seed-only is the TC's SearchQA section alone;
  - the other 9 are the 593-byte empty scaffold, or the scaffold plus one bullet (seed-rule 709 B, seed-rule3 1,016 B, cand 885 B, four placebos of about 780 B).
- So the cross-fitted best-of-11 figure (+5.5 items) measures switching per item from the TC to weaker texts. It is not a ceiling for rules added to the TC.
- The v3 rules are three proposals from the audited, defective v3 proposer. Their upper CI bounds reach +4.3 pts.
- Recommendation 1 cites the GLM line as "+2.9 n.s.". The ledger also has:
  - learned minus generic +4.6 [+0.5, +9.0] (gen17);
  - Skill learned from empty minus generic +6.7 [+2.5, +11.3] (fg17; same dev pool; GLM solver; 416-byte generic text).
- The ledger itself says "未建立，不是已证明没有" ("not established", not "proven absent").
- What the evidence supports: no gain was detected, and effects above about 5 pts look unlikely. It does not support a 0-3 pt ceiling.

2. CLAIM (recommendation 2): "the evidence (cal-1 form-sentence arms 0 to −3 pts, best-of-11 +2.75) says the predictable part is small".
- Checked: answer-tag presence by arm over the 8,800 cal-1 cells.
- The form-sentence arms on the scaffold drop the <answer> tag in 23.7% (seed-rule), 34.5% (seed-rule3) and 39.0% (cand) of replies. The bare scaffold drops it in 10.2-10.9%, the TC in 0.1%.
- Tagged replies in those arms pass 73%, 73% and 77% (scaffold 74%). Untagged replies pass 47-53%.
- So their deficits are confounded with format compliance, on a scaffold that lacks the TC's tag instruction. (This split is on a post-treatment variable, so it is descriptive only.) They say nothing about whether answer form is predictable.

3. CLAIM (recommendation 4): "Larger nominal headroom elsewhere is mostly noise or knowledge: flaky 27-40% and dead 38-78% ... optimistic ceiling of about 10 pts each".
- Checked: the explorer's analysis2/3 logs, and the 283-item LiveMath training pool, which I re-read on the new machine.
- On LiveMath, 58 of the 68 "dead" failed runs (85%) are D1 meta-option misses. The meta option is the reference in 129/129 training items that offer it; its letter is spread A23/B24/C28/D20/E34. That mass is reachable by an instruction in principle (a policy call for D7); it is not missing knowledge.
- Flaky mass (items the TC passes in some runs) is exactly where a text can raise the per-item pass probability, so discarding it as noise is unjustified.
- The other-text ceilings are 10.8 / 14.0 / 9.9 pts, so "about 10 each" understates LiveMath.
- The dead/other-text labels rest on a median of only 2-9 distinct other texts.
- The explorer's own pilot shows that "dead" does not mean unfixable.

4. CLAIM (paper advice): the headroom ladder (+22.75 / +18.4 / +11.4 / +2.75 / 0-1.5) "turns the v3 null into a measured ceiling effect".
- Checked: I read, by hand, the modal cal-1 TC answer against the reference for all 54 TC-failed SearchQA training items. This is a single-rater judgement.
- About 41 items (33.25 of 45.25 failure item-equivalents, about 73%; about 70% if two borderline cases are moved) are substantively acceptable answers that strict exact match rejects:
  - extra or missing qualifiers: "Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip" for "Studio 60", "Isaac Newton" for "Sir Isaac Newton", "Mike Huckabee" for "Huckabee";
  - plural: "fungus" for "Fungi";
  - diacritics: "Václav Havel";
  - the normalizer deleting a hyphen: "Marie-Antoinette" becomes "marieantoinette";
  - J! Archive optional parentheses: "(Sir Francis) Drake". 3 of the 4 parenthetical references are TC failures.
- Only about 13 items (12.0 item-equivalents, about 6 pts) are substantive errors.
- So the upper rungs of the ladder measure headroom in matching the reference string, not instruction headroom.

5. CLAIM (verdict_cn): "这里只能证明'不变差'，证明不了'更好'" ("only non-inferiority can be shown here, not superiority").
- This holds only for 200-item panels.
- With the registered 600-item SearchQA pool, the 4-run MDE is 2.6 pts (SD 0.2255, recomputed). By the explorer's own figure, +3 pts needs about 420 items, roughly 13M tokens.

6. Hidden cost (design field): "(a) ... otherwise k texts × 4 runs" is not costed.
- cal-1 alone hit its 25M-token cap at 7,189 of 8,800 cells (about 30M in total).
- OfficeQA: 3,256 cells, about 26-33M tokens.
- LiveMath: 4,400 cells, about 17M.
- ALFWorld: 2,508 episodes × about 105k, about 263M.
- Component (c) is uninformative by the explorer's own result (49/55 hints give the answer alone).
- Component (b) has no defined analog beyond SearchQA. For LiveMath, "which option class" is the answer itself.
missing:
- The OfficeQA half of D9 was never run, though the direction names SearchQA/OfficeQA.
  - OfficeQA sits in all three registered "similar" pairs.
  - Its TC pass rate is 25-29%, with substantive codes: D2 37%, D1 27%, D3 18%.
  - The explorer's estimate was about 2.5M tokens.
- There is no semantic-correctness audit separating scorer strictness from real errors: two raters or an LLM judge over the 54 failed items plus a sample of passes, about 0.2M tokens.
  - Literature: Kamalloo et al., ACL 2023, found that more than 50% of lexical-match failures are semantically equivalent answers.
  - SearchQA references are J! Archive responses (Dunn et al. 2017, arXiv:1704.05179).
  - Fixing the normalizer (diacritics, hyphen deletion, optional parentheses) is a decision for a new protocol version, not learning.
- No strong "TC + rule" candidates were tested. A literal ceiling over "any text" cannot be identified from finitely many tests. What can be measured:
  - the share of substantive errors;
  - the predictability probe (0.35M tokens; proposed but not run);
  - the cross-fitted best of a pre-registered set of TC + rule candidates.
- Transfer goes undiscussed. Rules that copy J! Archive answer conventions are unlikely to carry over to OfficeQA, so SearchQA cannot be the source of the transfer story either.
- LiveMath is not split into meta and non-meta items. On non-meta items the TC passes 62/110 runs (about 24 item-equivalents of failure mass over 55 items); that is the substantive headroom.
- Prompt-format sensitivity literature for the placebo spread is not cited: Sclar et al. 2023 report gaps of up to 76 accuracy points from formatting changes.
- The length hint counts words after punctuation removal ("Funk & Wagnalls" counts as 2 words, "Coca-Cola" as 1). This can mislead the solver and biases that arm slightly downward.
notes_cn: 数字都核对过，对得上：提示小试验、校准实验各文字总分、噪声大小、上一版规则效果，数学选择题里“可证明更强结论”选项在129道训练题里全是正确答案；也没读测试题。但“任务说明已接近任何通用文字的上限、规则最多多0到3分”不成立：拿来比的11种文字里9种只是空模板加一句话，没有一种是“任务说明再加一条规则”；早先换另一个模型时，学到的文字比通用指令高4.6到6.7分。我逐题看了任务说明答错的54道检索问答题：约四分之三意思其实对，只是写法和标准答案不同（头衔、单复数、重音符号、连字符、括号里可省的部分），真正答错的约6分。所以余量主要是评分写法，学到也难迁移到文档问答；文档问答这一半没做。
